sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever felt stuck in a loop you couldn't escape? Today we'll learn how to control loops like a pro!

• How to exit loops early with `break`
• How to skip to the next iteration with `continue`
• When to use each keyword effectively

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're searching for your favorite book in a library:

- `break` is like finding the book and immediately leaving the library
- `continue` is like skipping a shelf that doesn't have your book and moving to the next one

**The `break` keyword**
• Immediately exits the current loop
• Program continues with the next statement after the loop
• Works with `for`, `while`, and `do-while` loops

**The `continue` keyword**
• Skips the current iteration and jumps to the next one
• The loop condition is re-evaluated
• Only skips the current cycle, doesn't exit the loop

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: break immediately exits the enclosing loop and continues after it
continue skips the remaining body of the current iteration and proceeds to the next
Both break and continue apply only to the innermost enclosing loop
Excessive use of break and continue can make loop logic harder to follow
A break in a switch statement exits the switch, not an enclosing loop

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: `break` exits loops completely - use when you're done. `continue` skips to the next iteration - use to filter data. Practice using both in simple loops first. Ready to learn about nested loops next.
